cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a turquoise satin three-piece Baluchi women's outfit (dress, trousers, shawl) with the characteristic long chest pocket and dense colorful hand embroidery in diamond/snowflake motifs, matching known Baluchi dress traditions.

physical.title: dress
physical.summary: Baluchi-style woman's long-sleeve dress (dishdasha or pashk) made of turquoise-green satin silk that falls just below the knee; part of a three-piece outfit. The dress gathers at either side of the waist and, like other Baluchi-style dresses, is characterised by a long A-shaped pocket (pado pandohl) stitched on the front of the skirt below the chest panel (jig) to the top of the hem. The pocket is open along one of the short edges. The dress is densely hand-embroidered with colourful bands, diamond-shapes and snowflake patterns on the chest panel, long front pocket and sleeve cuffs, mainly in box-stitch. Colourful embroidered snowflake patterns are also scattered throughout the dress on the front and back. Worn with matching baggy silk trousers (sirwal, 2011,6003.44b) and silk head-shawl (shadar) (2011,6003.44c).
